label: confirmed
label_rationale: Out-of-bounds WRITE: the Edit path copies BodySize bytes into a chunk buffer allocated for a size chosen by an earlier packet, so a later packet can specify more. Heap overflow. ProcessPacket reads the packet's 16-bit BodySize field and memcpy's that many bytes without validating it against either how much data actually arrived or the size of the destination buffer. Confirmed against the target's own source, which ships as a wtf example; the pipeline itself only ever saw Ghidra pseudo-C.

notes: no module map was supplied, so 'wild' cannot be decided -- an address inside an unlisted system DLL would look wild when it is not
the fault is not attributable to the target module, so its bytes cannot be read from the binary on disk and no disassembly is available -- a system DLL in the guest may differ from any copy here
no registers: a crash file carries only its name and the test-case bytes, so register-derived judgements need CP8's replay stage

replay.notes: faulted at 0x7ff8aa3812de on 3/3 run(s) | every replay produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL rip trace, so the whole execution matched, not just the fault address -- the strongest determinism evidence bochscpu can give
